research.summary: The existing renderer hosts share the same Asset Library browser state and detail presenters but duplicate the page components. The current two-column CSS keeps cards in a vertical list and places selected details beside it, while fixed toolbar tracks overflow until a single breakpoint. The shared ModalDialog already owns focus containment, Escape, stacking order, accessible naming, and focus restoration, so detail cards can open loading, error, unavailable, and success content without new modal infrastructure. The browser state needs request sequencing to prevent late asynchronous reads from replacing a newer selection. The bounded JSON .aisb-package v1 contract and real inspector can support a deterministic client-side starter; a Blob/object-URL download requires no server or IPC operation and performs no package inspection, installation, activation, network access, or execution.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A workspace can search and select exact eligible built-in or system, admitted installed imported, and authored asset versions with truthful unavailable reasons for unsupported targets.

Creating, editing, publishing, failing, or abandoning a customization never changes the selected base definition, implementation release, package, authored record, or system-owned source.
Unchanged semantic fields and source files remain referenced by exact base identity while only modified fields and files create new customization entries before materialization.
Review materialization validates containment, sizes, allowed extensions, dependencies, capabilities, secret-like content, digests, and optimistic revisions before producing an immutable snapshot.
Publishing produces a distinct workspace-owned asset lineage with explicit provenance and no implicit build, release, installation, activation, deployment, or execution.
No customization fields are editable until a specific eligible exact asset version is selected, and changing the target requires explicit confirmation that clears incompatible work.
The workflow shows all important authorized semantic and implementation internals, distinguishes editable, protected, reused, and changed content, and explains why protected fields cannot be edited.
Users complete selection, definition, interfaces and configuration, implementation, and review and create sections in a predictable ordered interface consistent with other workflow features.
Successful completion visibly creates a new workspace-owned asset and leaves the base unchanged; errors preserve recoverable draft work and expose safe remediation.

research.summary: The accepted layered model can reuse immutable implementation artifacts, source snapshots, Asset Studio validation limits, structured authoring persistence, and existing definition/release repositories. Current target readers are intentionally unavailable, package admission retains exact facet artifacts without an aggregate editable source snapshot, and system defaults expose closed declarative implementation descriptors rather than repository source. The repository's resource-backed asset model is a separate catalog concept; customization should present source and bundle artifacts as implementation backing resources. Because non-system implementation release publication requires a successful qualified build, publishing a customization must create a distinct workspace-owned definition plus implementation draft and reviewed source snapshot, while build, implementation release, binding, activation, deployment, and execution remain separate explicit gates.
